identityReview: Gavin Christopher Newsom, born 10 October 1967 in San Francisco, Democratic governor of California since the 7 January 2019 inauguration; previously mayor from 8 January 2004 until the 10 January 2011 lieutenant-governor oath, then lieutenant governor until 2019. The second gubernatorial inauguration was 6 January 2023. Distinguish governor from governor-elect, elected governor from temporary acting-governor arrangements during travel, and current office from an anticipated 2027 transition. Use Santa Clara political-science degree in 1989 without resolving conflicting BA/BS shorthand.
lifeStatusEvidence: The governor’s 17 November 2026 report explicitly states that he met Republican and Democratic congressional leaders in Washington that day to seek wildfire recovery funds. AP and the state’s 16 November reporting independently corroborate the actual 15 November Lviv visit. These are completed activities, not a future itinerary or a photo merely reused in a later article.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read State Library and NGA profiles, CNN’s KTVZ chronology, the contemporaneous mayoral oath report, the official 2011 successor-mayor motion, the certified recall summary, the second-term inauguration release and selected prepared remarks, SB 53 and climate/housing signing releases, HCD fact-sheet introductory scope and approval sections, CalMatters’s execution-moratorium report, official and AP reporting on Lviv, and the 17 November congressional-meetings release. Read Commons portrait metadata/licensing/history and the linked current lieutenant-governor homepage. No video or image-pixel review performed.
corrections: Read the California State Library biography and its speech-date list. It confirms Gavin Christopher Newsom’s birth on 10 October 1967 in San Francisco, 1989 political-science graduation from Santa Clara, a partial baseball scholarship, a 1992 retail wine shop, 1997 appointment to the Board of Supervisors, and subsequent statewide election history. The original business was a San Francisco retail shop, not a winery first established in Oakville. Educational sources differ on BA versus BS, so retain the verified political-science degree without a degree-type abbreviation. Election in 2003 is not the 2004 mayoral oath, and election in 2018 is not the 2019 gubernatorial oath. The speech index supplies dates, not a read of every speech.

Read the National Governors Association’s current-governor profile. It confirms Democratic Party affiliation, date of birth, prior mayoral and lieutenant-governor roles, and lists inauguration dates of 7 January 2019 and 6 January 2023. The second entry is used for the inauguration ceremony, not an independently determined constitutional term-start calculation. Praise of his leadership and policy agenda is advocacy-style profile language, not an independent evaluation of success. Family details were not necessary to the public dossier.

Read CNN Editorial Research’s 4 May 2026 chronology syndicated on KTVZ. It supports the 1996 commission appointment, 1997 supervisor appointment, 1998 election, 2003 mayoral election and 2007 re-election, 2004 marriage-licence episode and subsequent invalidation, 2010/2014 lieutenant-governor elections, 2018/2022 gubernatorial elections, and pandemic-era restaurant attendance and apology. Its BS label is not chosen over conflicting BA descriptions elsewhere; use the degree and year established by the state library. The 2004 ruling on municipal authority did not itself determine all subsequent constitutional marriage questions. The 2020 conduct is recorded as a documented political controversy and apology, not a criminal finding. Private relationship history and medical details were not necessary and were omitted.

Read Rachel Gordon’s contemporaneous 8 January 2004 mayoral-inauguration account. Newsom took the oath that day as the 42nd mayor, succeeding Willie Brown after the December runoff. His housing and homelessness priorities were stated goals, not completed outcomes. Youngest in a century is not youngest mayor ever; no superlative is carried into the profile. The story’s comments about future bonds and staffing are not treated as implemented measures, and older family references are not current marital-status evidence.

Read the Board of Supervisors motion appointing Edwin Lee and its adoption record. It explicitly records Newsom’s completed lieutenant-governor oath at 1:25 p.m. on 10 January 2011, creating the mayoral vacancy. The motion was passed on 11 January, while a draft footer says 4 January and an earlier nomination meeting was 7 January; none replaces the 10 January oath date. The vacancy confirmation overrides shorthand biographies ending his mayoralty in 2010. The source does not establish that Lee’s later full term began at the time Newsom was sworn in.

Read the secretary of state’s final one-page recall summary. It records 7,944,092 no votes (61.9%) and 4,894,473 yes votes (38.1%) on the recall question and explicitly says Newsom remained in office. Percentages for the replacement-candidate question have a different denominator and cannot be treated as a direct two-person contest against him. Surviving recall continued his existing term; it was not a new four-year election. The underlying statewide certification materials were not comprehensively audited beyond this official summary.

Read the 6 January 2023 inauguration notice and relevant portions of the prepared address. The release reports a completed second-term inauguration; the remarks are labelled prepared, so not every written line is certified as delivered. The 8 November 2022 election is separately corroborated by CNN. The ceremony’s anniversary and political criticism of opponents are not independent findings about every policy dispute. Do not turn this ceremonial date into a separate calculation of the legal commencement of the constitutional term.

Read the 29 September 2025 SB 53 signing release, including its What the law does section. It identifies Senator Scott Wiener as author, Newsom as signer, large-frontier-developer framework disclosure, critical-safety-incident reporting and whistleblower protection. This is state legislation, not a federal statute, and publication of a framework does not certify any model as safe. CalCompute is a consortium and planning framework, not proof that a public compute cluster was already operational. Promotional claims about being the birthplace of AI or first in the nation and company valuation statistics are not adopted. The final statute, agency implementation and later litigation were not separately reviewed.

Read the 16 September 2022 climate-signing announcement and the AB 1279 section. It codifies a goal of statewide carbon neutrality no later than 2045. Projected jobs, economic savings, pollution reductions and future clean-energy targets are forecasts or policy commitments, not achieved results. The governor acted with the legislature; the programme is not his sole personal invention. No claim about the present legal status of the separate 2035 vehicle regulation or every oil-setback provision is inferred from this historical release.

Read the 16 September 2021 housing-package announcement, including SB 9’s duplex/lot-split purpose. SB 8, SB 9 and SB 10 are distinct bills; SB 10’s voluntary city zoning process is not silently attributed to SB 9. Funding and estimated unit counts are plans, not an independently measured number of completed homes. Approval reform is not proof that homelessness ended or housing affordability was restored. Detailed current eligibility is bounded by the housing department’s fact sheet rather than treating all parcels as eligible.

Read the September 2024 HCD fact sheet’s executive summary, single-family-zone scope and ministerial-review definition. It confirms environmental, tenant and historic-property conditions and describes approval without discretionary review for eligible projects. Up to four units from a split-and-duplex combination is not an unconditional permission on every parcel; an ADU is also not interchangeable with every primary unit. The profile keeps the general conditional reform and omits detailed current entitlement advice. The full statutory amendments and later case law were not audited; only the specified fact-sheet sections were reviewed.

Read CalMatters’s report, including its explicit 13 March 2019 update. The page’s original 12 March publication and 2020 modification are not the execution-order date. It describes a moratorium on executions, continuing imprisonment and death sentences, and political objections from supporters of capital punishment. The action was not repeal of the death penalty, a pardon or automatic commutation/release. The then-current 737-prisoner count is not a 2026 count and is omitted. The original order, every individual case and later statewide death-penalty developments were not comprehensively reviewed.

Read the governor’s 16 November 2026 Lviv release. It records an actual Sunday 15 November visit, meetings with regional officials, a cemetery visit and rehabilitation-related activities, and announces surplus medical equipment and supplies through a humanitarian partner. Publication on Monday is distinct from the Sunday visit; the dossier records 16 November public reporting of the aid arrangements. Announced donations are not proof that every bed, generator or bandage had arrived. Earlier 2022 shipments are separate from the new package. No claim of speaking for the federal government or independently inspecting delivery records is made.

Read the relevant body of AP’s 16 November 2026 report. It corroborates the Sunday Lviv visit and Monday announcement and describes a possible 2028 presidential run as under consideration. It does not establish a formal presidential candidacy or that his governorship had already ended. Delivery quantities and geopolitical claims outside the biographical scope are not adopted as independently verified outcomes. The source serves as independent corroboration of recent travel, not an audit of every statement in the governor’s announcement.

Read the 17 November 2026 official report of completed Washington meetings with lawmakers of both parties. The purpose was a supplemental recovery request for the January 2025 Los Angeles fires that remained unapproved by Congress. This is not evidence that funds were appropriated or received, nor that no other aid had ever been provided. The caption describes Jeffries as a future speaker, while the body correctly identifies his current minority-leader role; do not install him in a future office. Exact claimed permit, insurance and recovery figures and the attached letters were not independently reviewed. The completed meetings are the latest personal-activity evidence used here.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified native-language human review or legal advice. No original academic credential, full marriage judgment, original execution order, complete statutes/current case law, comprehensive budgets, housing outcome audit, physical aid-delivery records, video recordings, attached November congressional letters or portrait pixels were reviewed. Current office and completed recent activities are supported, but future candidacy, funding approvals, donations, housing production and emissions targets are not presented as achieved outcomes. Refresh political and implementation developments before publication.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons description, California-government public-records rationale and full upload history. The record describes a lieutenant-governor portrait dated 10 January 2011, not a new 2019 or 2026 gubernatorial portrait. Tktru first uploaded a 320×353 version on 17 January 2011, a 480×720 version on 5 February 2011 and the current 1365×2048 higher-resolution version on 3 October 2012. The current page lists 462 KB, while the old evidence cache records different byte metadata; neither cached bytes nor current pixels are available for comparison. The credit belongs to the lieutenant governor’s office, not the uploader. Commons uses a state-government-work rationale with exceptions, not the U.S. federal-work rule or a CC BY licence. Its linked current ltg.ca.gov homepage now concerns Eleni Kounalakis and does not itself reproduce the historical source chain. Original image request on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; referenced cached JPEG is absent. Historical source correspondence, exact capture date beyond metadata, identity, colour and resolution require further verification before publication.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and the English intermediary. Preserve degree/year without BA/BS expansion; retail shop versus winery origins; appointed versus elected supervisor; election versus inauguration; 2011 oath versus subsequent mayoral appointment motion; recall-question votes versus replacement-candidate votes and continuation versus new term; ceremonial second inauguration versus legal term calculation; 2004 invalidated marriage licences versus later marriage equality; execution reprieve versus repeal/pardon/release; SB 9 eligibility and policy aims versus built homes; AB 1279 target versus achieved neutrality; SB 53 state scope, large frontier developers and safeguards versus federal law or proven model safety; Lviv visit date versus release date; completed congressional meetings versus unapproved aid; possible 2028 bid versus formal candidacy.
